question: Which of the following is parenchyma type and present in aquatic plants, with large air cavities to help them float?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerenchyma** is a specialized type of **parenchyma** tissue characterized by the presence of **large air cavities** or intercellular spaces.
 
• It is primarily found in **aquatic plants** (also known as **hydrophytes**), such as **Lotus**, **Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia)**, and **Hydrilla**.
 
• The main function of these air cavities is to provide **buoyancy** to the plant, which helps them **float** on or near the water surface. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• Beyond buoyancy, **aerenchyma** also facilitates the **internal diffusion of gases** like **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide** between the aerial parts and the submerged tissues, which is vital for **respiration** and **photosynthesis** in an aquatic environment.
 
• The cells in this tissue are typically thin-walled and arranged in a way that creates a **sponge-like** network within the **cortex** of roots and stems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorenchyma**: 
 
 
• This is a type of **parenchyma** that contains **chlorophyll** and is responsible for performing **photosynthesis**.
 
• It is commonly found in the **mesophyll** of **leaves** and the outer green layers of **herbaceous stems**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Tracheid**: 
 
 
• **Tracheids** are elongated, tube-like cells that form a part of the **xylem** (complex permanent tissue).
 
• These cells are **dead at maturity**, have **lignified** walls, and are responsible for the **conduction of water** and minerals in vascular plants. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Companion Cell**: 
 
 
• These are specialized **parenchymatous cells** located in the **phloem** and are always associated with **sieve tube elements**.
 
• They possess a dense cytoplasm and a large nucleus to help regulate the **pressure gradient** and metabolic activities required for the **translocation of food**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parenchyma**: It is the most common **simple permanent tissue** in plants, consisting of relatively unspecialized cells with **thin cellulose walls**. They are **living cells** and serve functions like **storage**, **secretion**, and **support**.
 
• **Plant Tissue Classification**: 
 
 
• **Meristematic Tissues**: Responsible for growth through active **cell division** (Apical, Lateral, and Intercalary).
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissues**: Composed of a single type of cell (**Parenchyma**, **Collenchyma**, and **Sclerenchyma**).
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissues**: Composed of more than one type of cell working together as a unit (**Xylem** and **Phloem**).
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**: Provides **mechanical support** and **flexibility** to parts like the **petiole** of a leaf, allowing them to bend without breaking.
 
• **Sclerenchyma**: Consists of **dead cells** with very thick **lignin** deposits, providing **rigidity** and strength to the plant body (found in **husk of coconut**).
</ul
